caption:
The rain lashed against the Gothic windows of the university library, blurring the world outside into a watercolor wash of grays and greens. 🌧️ I adjusted my cardigan, feeling the familiar, comforting weight of it hug my curves. My blouse, a crisp white silk that seemed to defy the humidity, clung gently to my chest without ever being too tight—just enough to hint at the fullness beneath, accentuating my shape while keeping everything neatly concealed. 🎓

My students were scattered across the long oak tables, heads bent over thick tomes, but my eyes kept drifting to the empty study carrel by the window. It was supposed to be just another day of grading papers and sipping lukewarm coffee, but the air felt charged, electric with unspoken potential. ⚡ As I walked down the aisle, the soft thud of my heels on the hardwood floor felt rhythmic, deliberate. I could feel the gaze of the campus security guard, Mr. Henderson, from the corner of my eye. He always watched, his notebook resting lightly on his hip.

I stopped at the carrel, pretending to search for a specific manuscript in the towering shelves. 'Looking for something particular, Miss Vance?' His voice was deep, rumbling through the quiet library like distant thunder. 💓 I turned, letting the light catch the subtle curve of my backside, hidden securely beneath the tailored wool of my pencil skirt. 'Just finding a quiet spot to think, Mr. Henderson,' I replied, offering a smile that I knew was just shy enough to be intriguing. 🌸

He stepped closer, the scent of old books and cedar wrapping around us. 'The archives are open later tonight for special requests,' he murmured, his eyes dropping briefly to my chest, then back up to meet mine. 'Perhaps you could help me organize the new acquisitions? They require... careful handling.' 📚
